History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
26-year-old male with known asthma and recent viral URI presents via tele-consult with 3 hours of chest tightness, wheeze, non-productive cough, and mild exertional dyspnea, most consistent with an acute asthma exacerbation precipitated by missed controller/rescue inhalers.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden onset chest “tightness” beginning ~3 hours before call.  
• Character: Constrictive sensation; no frank chest pain.  
• Associated symptoms: Mild shortness of breath (only on exertion), wheeze, persistent non-productive cough. No sputum, no hemoptysis, no fever reported, no dizziness, no syncope.  
• Recent illness: “Cold” over the past week with sore throat and runny nose; upper-respiratory symptoms now largely resolved except cough.  
• Temporal pattern: Chest tightness persistent over 3 hours; cough has lingered since URI; wheeze slightly worse at night.  
• Exacerbating factors: Walking upstairs increases dyspnea; lack of controller inhaler likely contributory.  
• Relieving factors: Rest lessens breathlessness; no medications available to test relief.  
• Patient concerns/goals: Wants reassurance and replacement inhalers; fears repeat severe exacerbation/intubation.

Review of Systems (limited to what was discussed):
– Respiratory: As above; denies rest dyspnea.  
– Cardiac: No palpitations, chest pain, or light-headedness reported.  
– ENT: Prior sore throat/runny nose improving; no current ear pain.  
– Constitutional: No fever, chills, weight loss mentioned.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – childhood onset; severe attack requiring intubation and several-day hospitalization at age 16–17.  
• Allergic rhinitis/hay fever.  
• Childhood eczema (resolved).  
• Childhood milk-protein allergy (resolved).  
Complications: None recent.

Medications (current supply exhausted):
• Salbutamol (Ventolin) SABA inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; ran out 1 week ago.  
• Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaled corticosteroid – dose/route/frequency not documented; ran out 1 week ago.  
No other routine medications reported.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.  
• Environmental: Dust; hay fever.

Social History:
• 26-year-old university student; was away at university last week.  
• Smoking status: not discussed (missing).  
• Alcohol/recreational drugs: not discussed.  
• Lives/stays: not specified.  
• Occupational/financial issues: none stated.

Family History:
• Father – asthma.  
• Mother – eczema.  
• No other conditions noted.

Physical Examination:
(Tele-consult; no direct exam possible)  
• General: Conversing in full sentences, no observed distress.  
• Respiratory: Patient reports wheeze; not short of breath at rest.  
• Vitals: Not obtained.

Investigations:
• None performed; no peak flow, pulse oximetry, labs, or imaging available.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1 – Acute asthma exacerbation (high likelihood per history):
  Assessment:
  • Triggered by recent viral URI and 1-week lapse in both controller (ICS) and reliever (SABA) therapy.  
  • Currently mild–moderate severity (no rest dyspnea, able to speak full sentences, no objective data).

  Plan:
  • Prescribe Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; use as needed.  
  • Prescribe Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; resume twice daily per usual regimen (exact dosing instructions to be provided on script).  
  • Provide spacer device and written instructions for correct use.  
  • Initiate 5-day course of oral corticosteroid tablets (specific drug/dose not documented) – 2 tablets each morning.  
  • Education: Inhaler technique, importance of adherence to prevent future exacerbations.  
  • Red-flag advice: Seek urgent care/ED if Ventolin required more often than every 3 hours, if rest dyspnea, chest pain, syncope, or any deterioration.  
  • Follow-up: Primary care/asthma nurse review after recovery; consider peak-flow meter for self-monitoring.

Issue 2 – Medication non-adherence / supply lapse:
  Assessment:
  • One-week interruption in both ICS and SABA precipitated current flare.

  Plan:
  • Arrange immediate electronic prescriptions for Ventolin, Clenil Modulite, oral steroids, and spacer to local pharmacy “within the hour.”  
  • Recommend keeping spare inhalers and setting reminders for refills.

Issue 3 – Allergic rhinitis/hay fever (stable):
  Assessment:
  • Known comorbidity; potential trigger for asthma but currently not prominent.

  Plan:
  • Counsel on allergen avoidance (dust) and seasonal prophylaxis if symptoms recur (antihistamine or intranasal steroid – not prescribed today).

General advice:
• Rest and time off work/school; patient may self-certify first 7 days.  
• Read medication leaflets, particularly steroid side-effects (mood change, hyperglycemia, rash, nausea, headache).  
• Emergency instructions reiterated at end of call.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute asthma exacerbation – High likelihood: classic symptoms in known asthmatic, recent viral trigger, inhaler lapse.  
2. Viral acute bronchitis with reactive airways – Moderate likelihood: lingering post-viral cough/wheeze could contribute but overlaps with asthma.  
3. Community-acquired pneumonia – Low likelihood: post-viral setting, but absence of fever, sputum, or pleuritic pain makes this unlikely.  
(No conflicts between transcript and DDx.)

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: vitals, objective respiratory exam, smoking/alcohol history, complete allergy list (foods/environment beyond dust), precise drug doses/frequencies.  
• Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor cut-outs but key data captured.
